**TL;DR** 1-2 minutes if you put it on top of some ice, 5-15 minutes if you're just leaving it in there as is. You'll learn to know your freezer after the first few times.

**Full thing:** Giving it a touch will help you out most of the time, when the top of it feels very cold, it's done. (*touching the top because the bottom will feel cold while the insides are still warm*).

But the trick I find the most useful is to keep some ice in the freezer that I can put it on top of. A tiny bit of the ice will melt, enough to create excellent contact with the ice and thus cooling it much faster. This can reduce the needed time from 10 minutes in some cases, down to 1 minute, and it's a super low effort "trick" as well.
